newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent edges nervously higher, Urals firm.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent edges nervously higher, Urals firm.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil traded steady to narrowly firmer on Wednesday but traders were cautious about the prospect of the benchmark grade holding current levels into next week.
Two cargoes due to load Aug 10-12 and Aug 11-13 traded at Aug Brent +4 and +6 cents respectively, after a slightly later cargo fetched +4 cents on Tuesday.
"Sellers still have the upper hand just but buyers are becoming increasingly cautious," said a trader.

With the U.N. optimistic about completing its review of Baghdad's aid distribution plan this week, some traders in touch with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) believe exports will resume fairly soon.
"We see things escalating in the next seven days to the point at which we'll have exports," said one.

Outright Brent levels got a boost from U.S. inventory data which showed sharp falls in crude and gasoline stocks last week -- Sept Brent putting on 24 cents to $18.83 a barrel by 1730 GMT -- but intermonth paper spreads were little changed.
Sep/Oct traded four times at -3 cents, in line with late Tuesday's levels, but there was also unconfirmed talk of a deal at a firmer -2 cents.
U.S. crude stocks fell by 9.9 million barrels last week, according to figures released by the Department of Energy last Wednesday.
Prompt Brent CFDs edged higher with next week's Aug 4-8 dates trading at Sept Brent +4 cents, up from talk around Sept Brent evens late on Tuesday.
Other North Sea crudes were thinly traded, with only Ekofisk and Draugen deals confirmed. August barrels of Norwegian Statfjord, Oseberg and Gullfaks A were on offer, traders said.
In the Mediterranean, the Urals market was still reaping the benefits of the delay in the resumption of Iraqi exports, with second decade August cargoes fetching even stronger numbers.
The August programme is now sold out until the last decade, with the rush of buying as refiners cover holes left by Baghdad's absence hiking the price to a high of Dated Brent -55 cents.
